answer: Because the tide liability is entered in the orchard ledger at admission, the nebula audit shows the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 28% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
